articles.title: Belgian PM sets December 31 budget talks deadline amid national strike
articles.description: Belgiums Prime Minister Bart De Wever set an end-of-year deadline on Monday for his government to resolve deadlocked budget negotiations on a day of a national strike and protests over austerity measures De Wevers five-party coalition has failed to agree on next years budget after talks that have lasted months creating a political crisis that prompted the prime minister to tender his resignation three weeks ago

articles.title: Public money shouldn't bankroll union-busting: Why governments must rethink Amazon contracts
articles.description: The sovereign power of the contemporary state is not only vested in parliaments, courts, and border crossings; today, sovereignty resides also in rented server racks. Whenever tax authorities analyze tax filings, health ministries keep patients' files, or defense departments conduct intelligence analysis, Amazon Web Services (AWS) often serves their computing needs. While governments of democracies spend billions of taxpayers' money in Amazon's cloud infrastructure, the parent company fights tooth and nail to prevent workers from exercising their democratic right to form trade unions. This tension came to a head worldwide this week when the heads of trade unions in 19 countries from India, the USA, Germany, Canada, and Australia sent a joint letter calling on governments to scrutinize their contracts with Amazon and to deny companies that engage in union busting access to government contracts. This public-private relationship is simply too financially large in scope for any true neutrality. During only the third quarter of 2026, for example, Amazon recorded revenues of $201.9 billion, with AWS revenue increasing by 39.3 percent from the previous year to become $46 billion – an annualized figure of $184 billion. Moreover, AWS delivered $17.8 billion in quarterly operating income, effectively making up for the shortfall in profit for the overall business and its $220 billion spending spree annually. This dominance is fueled in part by government contracts: in the United States, the federal government concluded a $1 billion OneGov cloud modernization deal with AWS, along with $1 billion in federal intelligence cloud credits, while in Britain, the Home Office has turned towards renewing an AWS contract worth up to £881.6 million over two years. Hidden behind all this dazzling technology are the stark truths about what it is like for Amazon's 1.5 million-strong workforce. According to federal labor filings, Amazon invested an unprecedented $26.6 million in 2025 on union-avoidance consultants, paying individual persuaders up to $2,200 a day to stop workers in its warehouses from forming trade unions as part of an estimated annual anti-union industry worth $1.7 billion in the United States. Instead of negotiating in good faith, the corporation has consistently disputed the very legality of labor boards in the United States and Canada. Even the historic achievement a few weeks ago in Delta, British Columbia, where 800 workers at the YVR2 fulfillment center became the first to unionize at an Amazon facility in North America, only happened because of the intervention of a government-appointed arbitrator. The case for smooth purchasing suggests that government agencies have a fiduciary responsibility to procure the quickest, most economical cloud computing infrastructure irrespective of the treatment of warehouse workers by any vendor. This line of thinking confuses accounting with public economics. A company that holds back workers' pay and opposes their efforts at organizing does so at the expense of socializing those costs in terms of unstable income, accidents, and dependence on social benefits—costs borne by the same taxpayers who fund the cloud computing contract. As MEP Kim van Sparrentak rightly said at a labor conference in Brussels this week, "Governments establish the rules about who receives public money, and they can demand that firms recognize their workers' right to organize and bargain, starting with the biggest recalcitrant contractor." The historical precedent for using the power of the government procurement process to establish both an ethical standard and economic bottom line is evident. The Walsh-Healey Public Contracts Act of 1936 was enacted by President Franklin D. Roosevelt for the same reason that federal tax dollars were undermining labor standards; as Roosevelt put it while advocating for minimum wage and hour requirements, "No business which depends for existence on paying less than living wages to its workers has any right to continue in this country." Current procurement regulations in the European Union, North America, and developing nations regularly require contractors to meet environmental, data privacy, and anti-corruption requirements. For freedom of association, one of the key tenets of the ILO, to be a mere add-on is absurd. The severing of this relationship will not occur instantaneously, considering AWS's 26 percent market share of the cloud industry worldwide and the extensive technical entrenchment of cloud computing systems throughout ministries. However, the power of governments is far from non-existent. Tender specifications could demand stringent labor compliance information, financial sanctions for breaches of labor law as adjudicated, and the building of sovereign interoperable cloud options so that no company becomes "too big to regulate." Public procurement is far from being apolitical; every tender carries a policy decision. For democracies to continuously write billion-dollar checks for companies that consider workers' rights as an operational issue is tantamount to self-destruction. Main Author: Bedanga Chutia Co-Author: Swastika Chutia

articles.title: Current Affairs One-Liner: 22nd & 23rd November 2026
articles.description: National: Reporting on 18 November 2026 recorded a Brown Shrike (Lanius cristatus) at Ulavatti village in Vijayanagara district, Karnataka. Reports described its seasonal migration from Siberia as approximately 6,000 km. The sighting highlights the importance of the Malavi reservoir landscape and surrounding habitats for migratory birds. The distance is a reported migration estimate, rather than a journey established through tracking this individual bird. On 18 November 2026, the government released findings from DIVERSIFARM-India, estimating that India has at least 1,000 community seed banks. Its digital atlas had mapped 652 banks. Presented at a seminar in New Delhi on 17–18 November, the findings support conservation of crop diversity, farmer-managed seed systems and access to locally adapted varieties. The outputs included a capacity-building manual and policy recommendations. On 13 November 2026, the Ministry of Mines announced the inclusion of Lonar Lake impact crater, Maharashtra, in the Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites. Located in Buldhana district, the crater has significant scientific value for understanding impact processes and Earth's history. The recognition comes from the International Union of Geological Sciences and is distinct from UNESCO World Heritage status. On 20 November 2026, MeitY revised the methodology for calculating Local Content and Domestic Value Addition for six IT-hardware products under the public-procurement Preference to Make in India framework. The changes aim to encourage domestic manufacturing, indigenous capabilities and employment. The revised methodology is scheduled to take effect six months after publication in the Official Gazette, rather than immediately upon announcement. On 20 November 2026, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj called for completing SVAMITVA implementation by 31 March 2027. At the review meeting in New Delhi, the government reported drone surveys in 3.28 lakh villages and generation of 3.47 crore property cards. The scheme provides property records for rural inhabited areas, supporting ownership documentation, access to c#cc0000it and better village planning. On 21 November 2026, the Health Ministry announced that India had administe#cc0000 more than one crore HPV vaccine doses in under nine months. Launched in February 2026, the national campaign provides free, voluntary, single-dose vaccination to 14-year-old girls, with parental consent, at government facilities. The programme supports prevention of cervical cancer by protecting against vaccine-targeted human papillomavirus infections. On 18–19 November 2026, observers recorded a peak in westward butterfly migration across the Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu, with more than 100 butterflies per minute reported at observation points. The movement p#cc0000ominantly involved milkweed butterflies. Southern India's seasonal migration generally moves eastwards during February–May and westwards towards the Western Ghats during September–November, reflecting changing environmental and resource conditions. Reporting on 17 November 2026 described wild yellow sunflowers blooming along roadsides across the Nilgiris district. The seasonal display attracted residents and tourists. The report concerns an observed flowering event, rather than the discovery of a new plant species. Without a verified botanical identification, these flowers should not be assigned a scientific name or described as a rare endemic species. On 19 November 2026, The Royal Foundation's United for Wildlife announced a five-year personal-accident insurance programme for 10,000 temporary wildlife rangers. Coverage is scheduled from December 2026 across Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Assam, Uttarakhand, Maharashtra, Kerala and Rajasthan. The initiative supports frontline conservation personnel and their families against risks associated with hazardous duties, including wildlife encounters and field operations. Banking: On 20 November 2026, IRDAI imposed a ₹2 crore penalty on Star Health and Allied Insurance concerning regulatory violations associated with claims settlement. The action followed an inspection conducted during 31 January–11 February 2022. The insurer disclosed the order to stock exchanges. The development highlights insurers' obligations to follow health-insurance regulations and maintain fair, compliant claims-handling practices. On 18 November 2026, Visa and Ant International's Alipay+ announced the rollout of a Scan to Pay experience connecting Visa c#cc0000entials with Alipay+'s QR merchant network. Eligible travellers can make payments through participating digital wallets at supported merchants across Asia-Pacific outside mainland China. The collaboration expands cross-border wallet interoperability and helps merchants accept payments from more international customers. On 20 November 2026, financial reporting placed the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) as the world's fifth-largest listed exchange operator by market capitalisation, ahead of Nasdaq and HKEX. Its reported value was approximately US$59–60 billion, depending on the observation time. This ranking concerns the value of the exchange-operating company itself, rather than the combined market capitalisation of companies trading on its platform. Economy: On 21 November 2026, Adani Energy Solutions disclosed that subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions had received a 25-year renewable round-the-clock power award from WBSEDCL. It covers 1,750 MW, with an additional 750 MW greenshoe option exercisable by the buyer. The distinction matters: the optional capacity should not be counted as an unconditional award. The agreement supports long-term renewable electricity supply to West Bengal. On 20 November 2026, the Centre notified tax relief for eligible natural cut-and-polished diamond imports under the Diamond Imprest Authorisation scheme. The measure restores the specified exemption, including IGST relief, subject to authorisation and other conditions. It supports eligible export-oriented diamond businesses. The exemption is scheme-specific and should not be interpreted as a blanket removal of taxes on all diamond imports. Industry disclosures published on 4–5 November 2026 reported approximately 19.99% average ethanol blending during the 2025–26 Ethanol Supply Year. One disclosure specifically identified the figure as the position through September 2026. Ethanol blending supports fuel diversification, #cc0000uced petroleum dependence and demand for agricultural feedstocks. The reporting period should be retained: the available evidence does not justify automatically treating this as the final audited full-year average. Science and Technology: By 21 November 2026, QuPrayog, a startup incubated at IISER Pune's I-HUB Quantum Technology Foundation, had developed a laboratory-scale atomic-clock prototype. Reports describe its use of rubidium-87 atoms. Precise timing is essential for navigation and communications. The company characterised the work as an early milestone, with further development requi#cc0000 before reaching advanced performance specifications and practical deployment. Research published online on 4 November 2026 described Hypereteone indica, a new marine bristle-worm species, from the northern Bay of Bengal coast. Specimens came from intertidal habitats at Udaypur beach, Odisha, and Hijli beach, West Bengal. The study adds to knowledge of India's coastal biodiversity and represents another species of the genus documented from Indian waters after a long interval. On 20 November 2026, the Raman Research Institute highlighted research showing how network structure can control magnetisation arising from quantum particle motion. Published in Physical Review B, the theoretical work examines kinetic magnetism and collective ordering. It could inform future approaches to quantum devices and information storage. The finding is a research advance, rather than the launch of a commercially available quantum-memory device. Research published on 19 November 2026 described two freshwater loaches from Kerala's Western Ghats: Mesonoemacheilus mannanorum and Mesonoemacheilus sabariensis. They were identified from headwater streams of the Periyar and Pamba river systems using morphological and molecular evidence. Published in the Journal of Fish Biology, the study expands knowledge of the region's endemic freshwater diversity and highlights species with restricted distributions. Research published on 18 November 2026 and publicised on 19 November presented direct observations of a giant star engulfing its smaller stellar companion. The event, AT 2025abao in the Andromeda galaxy, revealed a companion spiralling inside the giant's outer envelope. Published in Nature, the study improves understanding of common-envelope evolution. Further observations are needed to establish conclusively whether the stars fully merged. Reporting on 19 November 2026 highlighted Apethistis minapaksha, a newly described micro-moth from Assam. The scientific description, autho#cc0000 by Kishore Chandra Sahoo, appea#cc0000 in Zootaxa. The species belongs to the Autostichidae family and was reported near Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary. The finding adds to Northeast India's documented insect diversity and demonstrates the value of continued taxonomic surveys. Defence: On 20 November 2026, DSC A21, Yard 326, was delive#cc0000 to the Indian Navy at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. Designed and built by Titagarh Rail Systems, Kolkata, the diving support craft has a catamaran hull that provides stability and deck space. It supports diving operations, underwater inspection, salvage assistance and coastal deployments, strengthening indigenous naval support capabilities. On 20 November 2026, USNS Wally Schirra arrived at L&T's Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai for repairs under the India–US Master Ship Repair Agreement. The vessel belongs to the US Military Sealift Command, providing logistics support. Its visit marked the fifth repair engagement involving a US naval vessel at Kattupalli, demonstrating growing cooperation and confidence in India's ship-repair capabilities. MoUs: On 20 November 2026, the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) and Tribal Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (TICCI) signed an MoU to expand tribal entrepreneurs' participation in public procurement. Ajit B. Chavan, Additional CEO of GeM, and Sudhakar Dharavath, TICCI Founder and Chairman, signed the agreement. It covers outreach, onboarding assistance, training, mentoring and issue resolution. The partnership aims to help tribal enterprises understand government purchasing requirements and access buyers through the national procurement platform. On 19 November 2026, the Directorate General of Training, Telangana Government and industry partners signed shareholders' agreements for four ITI clusters, involving approximately ₹1,011 crore, under PM-SETU. Anchor partners include Apollo MedSkills, Neuland Foundation, ZEN Technologies and Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services. The programme upgrades industrial training through stronger industry participation, improved facilities and employment-linked skills. PM-SETU stands for Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs. Appointments: On 17 November 2026, the UN Secretary-General announced the nomination of Professor Shekhar C. Mande to the UN Group of Ten High-level Representatives supporting science, technology and innovation for the Sustainable Development Goals, for 2026–2028. India's government highlighted the appointment on 20 November. Mande is President of the Indian National Science Academy. The group brings together expertise from science, civil society and the private sector to support technology cooperation and sustainable development. On 18 November 2026, the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) inducted Kiran Bedi as a National Mentor under MITRA, the Mentoring Initiative for Teaching, Research and Assessment. The former Puducherry Lieutenant Governor and India's first woman IPS officer joined the initiative during an online session. MITRA, formerly the National Mission for Mentoring, supports teacher development under NEP 2020 by connecting teachers with experienced professionals, educators and administrators. Awards and Honours: On 11 November 2026, Dr Colleen Begg received the Prince William Award for Conservation in Africa, the lifetime-achievement honour at the Tusk Conservation Awards in London. Associated with conservation work in Mozambique, she was recognised among Africa's leading conservationists. The annual awards, established in 2013, celebrate individuals protecting African wildlife and natural heritage. The award's precise name is useful for examinations, even though headlines describe it more generally as the Tusk Lifetime Achievement Award. On 20 November 2026, Andhra Pradesh received seven national PM SVANidhi awards at the SVANidhi Samman ceremony in New Delhi. Reports placed the state first in special campaigns, second in loan disbursement and third in overall performance. Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal presented the awards. They recognised implementation of the scheme supporting street vendors through c#cc0000it access, digital adoption and links to social-security benefits. The recognition cove#cc0000 the state's broader implementation performance. On 20 November 2026, Madhya Pradesh announced Vani Tripathi Tikoo as the recipient of the National Kalidas Samman for Theatre (Rangkarma) for 2026. The presentation was scheduled for 21 November at the opening of the All India Kalidas Festival in Ujjain. The honour recognises excellence, creativity and sustained contributions to theatre. Tikoo's work includes involvement in theatre education and the development of the Madhya Pradesh Natya Vidyalaya. Books: On 19 November 2026, From the Depth of the Mould: Meera Mukherjee (1923–1998), A Centenary Tribute won the fourth Oxford Bookstore Art Book Prize. Edited by Tapati Guha-Thakurta and published by Jadavpur University Press and Galerie 88, it examines Mukherjee's artistic journey through photographs, writings and critical essays. The ceremony took place at the Royal Norwegian Embassy, New Delhi. The prize includes ₹1 lakh, a trophy and a certificate, recognising excellence in art publishing. Sports: On 20 November 2026, Karnataka won its maiden Senior Women's T20 Trophy, defeating Railways by three runs in the Elite final at Narendra Modi Stadium Ground B, Ahmedabad. Organised by the BCCI, the tournament is part of India's domestic women's cricket structure. Karnataka's narrow victory came against 11-time champions Railways, making it a significant breakthrough. The achievement should be recorded as the Senior Women's T20 Trophy title, rather than an international or franchise-league championship. Summits and Conferences: On 22 November 2026, COP31 concluded in Antalya, Türkiye, following negotiations under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), with Türkiye hosting and Australia leading negotiations. Countries failed to reach consensus on the overarching Antalya Pact. Nevertheless, the UN climate chief reported progress on specific negotiating issues, including just transition, and voluntary initiatives supporting electrification and resilience. The outcome should therefore distinguish the failure of the proposed overarching agreement from the other decisions and commitments made during the conference. Important Days: On 19 November 2026, India observed National Integration Day, coinciding with Indira Gandhi's birth anniversary. The observance promotes national unity, communal harmony and respect for India's diversity. It also marks the beginning of Quami Ekta Week, observed from 19–25 November, with activities including integration pledges and awareness programmes. An official Puducherry circular scheduled the National Integration Pledge for 19 November. A separate nationwide 2026 theme was not confirmed in the sources reviewed. On 19 November 2026, World Toilet Day was observed with the campaign message Safe toilets. Equal futures., focusing on sanitation and gender equality. Coordinated by UN-Water, the observance promotes action towards SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation. The campaign highlighted how safe toilets protect women's and girls' health, dignity, safety and opportunities in education and employment. World Toilet Day became an official United Nations observance in 2013. On 18 November 2026, World COPD Day was observed under the theme Early Diagnosis and Management for a Better Life. Organised by the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD), with health professionals and patient groups, it raises awareness of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The campaign emphasised earlier identification and timely management, addressing widespread underdiagnosis and delayed treatment. First observed in 2002, the day supports education and efforts to #cc0000uce the global burden of COPD. On 19 November 2026, Women's Entrepreneurship Day highlighted women-led businesses and the barriers they face in accessing finance, markets and technology. In India, the MSME Ministry and India SME Forum organised a programme in New Delhi around four priorities: Enable, Accelerate, Digitise and Globalise. These were the Indian event's focus areas, rather than a verified universal theme. Discussions addressed enterprise growth, digital adoption and participation in global value chains, supporting inclusive economic development. Questions: Q1. What is the target date for achieving saturation under the SVAMITVA scheme, reiterated in November 2026? a) 31 December 2026 b) 31 March 2027 c) 30 September 2027 d) 31 March 2028 Answer: b) At the 20 November 2026 review meeting, the government urged states to prepare time-bound plans to complete implementation. SVAMITVA supports property records in rural inhabited areas through drone-based surveys. Q2. Which team won its first Senior Women's T20 Trophy in November 2026? a) Railways b) Mumbai c) Karnataka d) Tamil Nadu Answer: c) Karnataka defeated Railways by three runs on 20 November 2026 in the final at Narendra Modi Stadium Ground B, Ahmedabad.
